source.name: Theorems about the definitions of a co-occurrence matrix and the statistics of one, checked by Lean
source.how: each expected value is proved to be the value of the feature's definition at the doubles nearest the stored values, or within half a unit in its last place of it, by the theorem its record names in spec/XtractSpec/Records/Cooccurrence.lean; written by tests/reference/generate/lean_cooccurrence.py and checked by Lean's kernel

tolerance.reason: no rounding: the values sum to 16, and every share, every product and every sum of the products is a double, so each division, each multiplication and each addition is exact; the expected value is exact

no rounding: the values sum to 16, and every share, every square and every sum of the squares is a double, so each division, each multiplication and each addition is exact; the expected value is exact
no rounding: the values sum to 16, and every share, every quotient and every sum of the quotients is a double, so each division and each addition is exact; the expected value is exact

2050 roundings, each within 2^-53 relatively: the N - 1 additions of the values, of one sign, in any order, which every share has in common; the division of a value by their sum and the two multiplications by the difference of its row and its column, in every term; the N - 1 additions of the terms, of one sign, in any order; and the expected value

3073 roundings, each within 2^-53 relatively: the N - 1 additions of the values, of one sign, in any order, which every share has in common, and the division of a value by their sum, all of which the square of a share counts twice; the square, in every term; the N - 1 additions of the terms, in any order; and the expected value

2049 roundings, each within 2^-53 relatively: the N - 1 additions of the values, of one sign, in any order, which every share has in common; the division of a value by their sum and the division by 1 and the square of the difference of its row and its column, which is a whole number, in every term; the N - 1 additions of the terms, of one sign, in any order; and the expected value
no rounding: a count is a whole number and there are 16 pairs, a power of two, so each division is exact; the expected value is exact
2 roundings, each within 2^-53 relatively: the division of a count, which is a whole number, by the 1740 pairs; and the expected value
